title: Atlassian Rebuilds Metrics Pipeline Around OpenTelemetry at Massive Scale
gist: Atlassian migrated its metrics platform (about 100,000 hosts, 14 regions, 4.8B data points/minute) from gostatsd to OpenTelemetry Collector distributions while keeping the StatsD interface, cutting sidecar cost ~30%, halving aggregation CPU and turning an org-wide migration into a platform-team one.

insights.claim: Atlassian migrated a metrics platform receiving data from about 100,000 hosts across 14 regions from gostatsd to OpenTelemetry while maintaining a 99.95% SLO.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Large enterprises are standardising on OpenTelemetry, reinforcing it as the industry telemetry layer.

insights.claim: gostatsd's UDP-only design could not handle traces or logs, and staying on it would have meant reproducing features already being built by the OpenTelemetry Collector community.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Community-built open standards outcompete bespoke internal tooling.
insights.locator: In a post on the CNCF blog

insights.claim: By keeping the StatsD-over-UDP interface and rebuilding the pipeline behind it, Atlassian turned an organisation-wide application migration into a platform-team migration.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Compatibility layers lower migration cost and risk for observability platform switches.
insights.quote: We kept the interface and rebuilt everything behind it, which turned an org-wide migration into a platform-team migration.

insights.claim: Atlassian rolled out through development and staging, chose early adopters with something to gain, and then expanded through 1%, 10%, 50% and 100% stages.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: A replicable playbook for low-risk infrastructure migrations.

insights.claim: Small tests and benchmarks were insufficient; continuous profiling in production showed Atlassian where to optimise.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Supports demand for continuous profiling tools.
insights.quote: Small tests and benchmarks were not enough; continuous profiling in prod is what actually told us where to optimise.

insights.claim: Folding metrics into the existing tracing sidecar saved an average of 3.9% CPU per expensive Micros service and cut sidecar cost by about 30% across the fleet.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Consolidating telemetry agents yields material infrastructure savings.

insights.claim: The platform ingests about 4.8 billion data points per minute and stores about 220 million, a roughly 96% reduction via aggregation.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Aggregation dramatically reduces storage costs, pressuring per-datapoint pricing of observability vendors.

insights.claim: Atlassian built and open-sourced its own delta-metric aggregation processor, and the revised aggregation tier uses about half as much CPU for the same traffic.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Enterprise contributions are filling gaps in the OpenTelemetry ecosystem.

insights.claim: Hashing by stream ID with the OpenTelemetry contrib load-balancing exporter, instead of by service and environment, spread large services across the pool, giving more even CPU, fewer hot shards and better off-peak scaling.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Finer-grained sharding improves cost efficiency of stateful telemetry pipelines.
insights.locator: The ingest tier presented a different problem

insights.claim: gostatsd aggregation and nomad account for about 38% of CPU requests in Atlassian's metrics clusters, with nomad alone using about 13% of total resources, and removing them will complete the end-to-end OpenTelemetry pipeline.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Further cost savings remain to be captured.

insights.claim: A stateless Collector distribution called metrics-gateway fans data out to destinations including SignalFx and S3, making adding a destination a configuration change rather than an integration project.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: OpenTelemetry lowers switching costs between observability vendors, weakening vendor lock-in.
insights.locator: In the final stage, Atlassian replaced

insights.claim: Atlassian's next step is moving application instrumentation from StatsD, DogStatsD and vendor clients to OpenTelemetry SDKs.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Migration away from vendor-specific clients like DogStatsD reduces vendor stickiness.

insights.claim: Airbnb used dual emission and VictoriaMetrics' vmagent for streaming aggregation, processing more than 100 million samples per second, and Skyscanner moved over 300 microservices by updating a common library; all separated application migration from infrastructure replacement.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Several major tech companies are migrating to OpenTelemetry, signalling an industry-wide trend.
insights.locator: The approach differs slightly from Airbnb

insights.claim: GREE's Iwahori praised the approach but questioned scaling the stateful aggregation tier, and Atlassian's answer indicated that part relies on manual configuration.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Stateful aggregation remains an operational weak point.
